summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, neurogenic bladder, and bilateral below-knee amputations was readmitted one day after discharge due to fever and hypotension. She was diagnosed with sepsis likely from a urinary tract infection caused by pan-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. She was treated with intravenous meropenem for seven days and improved clinically with resolution of fever and normalization of labs. Her acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia resolved with fluid resuscitation and holding lisinopril. Blood and urine cultures eventually cleared. She was restarted on home medications including metoprolol, lisinopril, and gabapentin. Urology planned outpatient training in clean intermittent catheterization to reduce future UTIs. She was discharged home with nursing services, stable and afebrile, with follow-up arranged in urology, infectious disease, and primary care.
